plans.note: Section 15 is expressly one-sided ('Limitation of Garman's Liability'); review cap amount, mutuality and carve-outs for IP indemnity (sec-13), confidentiality (sec-14) and wilful misconduct. Check whether warranty remedies in sec-12 are subordinated to the cap.

IP indemnity sits in sec-13; confirm defence/settlement control, no unreasonable exclusions, and that it is not capped by sec-15. Look for absence of any broader vendor indemnity (personal injury, property damage, breach of confidentiality) and for any customer-side indemnity to keep narrow.

Software licence of this type rarely restricts the customer's business lines; scan sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) and sec-20 (General Matters) for any covenant limiting our ability to use or build competing routing systems before concluding absence.

Check the licence grant (sec-2), use restrictions (sec-3) and maintenance/support (sec-10) for any sole-source or exclusive-provider language (e.g. only Garman may maintain or modify the Software); otherwise no exclusivity binds us.
Fees (sec-11) is the only likely home for pricing parity language; verify no obligation on us to extend best terms to Garman. Note as absent if fees are fixed per Schedule.

Section 19 binds us on employee non-solicitation; check mutuality, duration (target 12 months post-termination), scope limited to individuals actually engaged under this Agreement, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out. Confirm whether sec-18 makes it survive.

Termination provisions are in sec-17, with reject/refund mechanics in sec-7 and sec-8. Confirm we may terminate maintenance (sec-10) on notice without penalty and that Garman has no convenience right or suspension right mid-term; check for termination fees in sec-11.

Maintenance term and any automatic annual renewal will sit in sec-17 and/or sec-10, with uplift mechanics in sec-11; test the non-renewal notice window (no more than 30-60 days) and cap any renewal price increase.

Governing law, venue and any dispute-resolution/arbitration clause should be in General Matters (sec-20); confirm it names an accepted jurisdiction and courts rather than foreign arbitration, and check for jury-trial waiver or venue inconvenient to us.

Assignment is normally in sec-20; also check sec-3 for restrictions on transferring the licence to affiliates or a purchaser of our business, and sec-17 for any termination trigger on our change of control.

Ownership statements likely in sec-2/sec-3 with source-code escrow in sec-16. Confirm our data, configurations and any converted data (sec-4) remain ours, that modifications/custom work we pay for do not vest solely in Garman, and that sec-14 protects our Confidential Information.

Grant scope in sec-2 read with definitions/Schedules (sec-1, Authorized Locations) and restrictions in sec-3; seek perpetual/irrevocable, affiliate and contractor/outsourcer use, and flexibility to add or relocate locations and users.

Any usage-verification or inspection right against us would appear in sec-3 or sec-20; if present, require prior notice, business hours, annual frequency, confidentiality and Garman's cost absent material under-licensing. Mark absent only after reviewing sec-3 in full.

Check sec-11 for interest/late-payment charges or non-refundable fee forfeiture and sec-17 for accelerated fees on termination; these are the likely customer-payable penalties. Confirm whether any service credits or acceptance-failure remedies run in our favour (sec-6, sec-10).

Section 12 carries specifications and warranty; test duration (target 12 months from acceptance), remedy (repair/replace then refund), and whether sec-15 disclaims implied warranties or caps the remedy. Cross-check acceptance testing (sec-6) and ongoing maintenance obligations (sec-10).

No insurance heading appears; Garman personnel will be on our sites for delivery/installation (sec-4) and implementation (sec-9), so if absent we should add commercial general liability, professional/E&O and cyber cover in sec-20.

Watch for committed multi-year maintenance fees or minimum licence/seat counts in sec-11, sec-10 or the Schedules referenced in sec-1; if a take-or-pay style commitment exists, pair it with a termination right.

Post-termination effects should be in sec-17 with survival in sec-18 and refund/return mechanics in sec-8; check for return of our data in usable format, continued escrow access (sec-16) and paid transition assistance. Likely thin and needing addition.
